## Philosophy quotes about happiness

Happiness—or flourishing—is a central aim in ethics: what makes a life go well, and whether pleasure alone is enough.

21 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

### Why this theme matters

Greek eudaimonia, Buddhist analyses of craving, utilitarian happiness, and modern well-being research all contest the meaning of a good life.

### In the history of philosophy

Aristotle, Epicurus, the Stoics, and Confucian flourishing ideals remain primary references; later utilitarianism reframed happiness as aggregable preference or pleasure.

[Aristotle](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/aristotle) , [Epicurus](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/epicurus) , [John Stuart Mill](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/john-stuart-mill) , [Albert Camus](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/albert-camus) , [Bertrand Russell](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/bertrand-russell) , [Jeremy Bentham](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/jeremy-bentham) , [Plato](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/plato) , [Thomas Hobbes](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/thomas-hobbes)

### Frequently asked questions

#### What is happiness in philosophy?

It may mean pleasure, desire satisfaction, or eudaimonic flourishing through virtue and meaningful activity.

#### Is happiness the same as pleasure?

Not for most virtue ethicists; pleasure can be part of a good life without exhausting it.
